entries.subject: Placement
entries.finding: Reardon et al. (2024), ApJL 971, L18, Table 1, PPTA-DR3 column: RA 04:37:15.9284042(4), Dec -47:15:09.303700(4) (J2000) at reference epoch MJD 55486, proper motion 121.4420(6), -71.4717(7) mas/yr (https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.07132): pulsar timing position at epoch J2010.7912. Distance: 156.98 +/- 0.15 pc from Reardon et al. (2024), ApJL 971, L18, Table 1, PPTA-DR3: distance from the Shklovskii effect on the orbital period (https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.07132). Radial velocity: -75 +/- 18 km/s from Reardon et al. (2024), ApJL 971, L18, Table 1, PPTA-DR2e: derived from the spin frequency's second derivative assuming no excess timing noise contributes to it; with another noise model the same paper finds -24 +/- 40 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.07132).

entries.subject: Radius and mass
entries.finding: Radius 11.36 km from Choudhury et al. (2024), ApJL 971, L20, Table A.1: equatorial radius 11.36 +0.95/-0.63 km (68% credible interval) from NICER pulse-profile modelling. Mass 1.418 solar masses from Reardon et al. (2024), ApJL 971, L18, Table 1, PPTA-DR3: pulsar mass from the Shapiro delay.

entries.subject: Hot regions
entries.finding: Choudhury et al. (2024)'s fit to NICER X-ray pulse profiles of 2017 to 2021, transcribed as science/choudhury-2024/hot-regions.json and drawn without refitting as the mean over 2,006 of the fit's 218,553 posterior samples (every 109th), so an edge is sharp where the samples agree and graded where they differ: 2 regions, 0.53 million K to 1.58 million K. The surface outside them is at 250,000 K: Qi et al. (2026), arXiv:2605.05429, Table 1 measure from Hubble far-ultraviolet and ROSAT soft X-ray spectra, fitted without hot regions (https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.05429).

entries.subject: Limb darkening
entries.finding: The disc is dimmed toward the limb by the quadratic law (u1 0.939, u2 0.029) fitted to the bolometric intensity of the NSX hydrogen atmosphere table nsx_H_v200804.out (Ho & Lai 2001, MNRAS 327, 1081; Ho & Heinke 2009, Nature 462, 71), distributed with X-PSI, at log g 14.26 and 250,000 K; least-squares fit to the table's 62 emission cosines of 0.05 and above; largest miss 0.003 of the centre intensity.

entries.subject: Spin
entries.finding: 173.6879456649439 turns a second, north pole 137.506 degrees from the line of sight, from Reardon et al. (2024), ApJL 971, L18, Table 1, PPTA-DR3: spin frequency, and the orbital inclination 137.506(16) degrees that Choudhury et al. (2024) use as the spin axis's inclination; the axis's direction on the sky is a convention.
